question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(3)(a), before a person may qualify for a Nebraska real estate broker's license, how much real estate salesperson experience must they generally have?
choice_a: One year of full-time experience as a licensed salesperson
choice_b: Two years of full-time experience as a licensed salesperson (or part-time equivalent)
choice_c: Three years of full-time experience as a licensed salesperson
choice_d: No prior salesperson experience is required if 60 additional education hours are completed
explanation: Nebraska's Real Estate License Act requires broker applicants to have two years of active, full-time licensed salesperson (or associate broker) experience, or the part-time equivalent, before they may qualify for a broker's license. This experience requirement works together with the additional 60 hours of pre-license education required of broker applicants. Applicants who cannot meet this standard may seek a hardship exception from the Commission.

question: In addition to satisfying the experience requirement, how many clock hours of Commission-approved pre-license coursework must a Nebraska broker applicant complete beyond what is required for a salesperson's license, per §81-885.13(3)(a)?
explanation: Broker applicants must complete 60 clock hours of pre-license education across two courses, in addition to the hours already required for a salesperson's license. One of those two courses is the 6-hour Professional Practice and Standards course (#0003), which does not need to be repeated if it was already completed for the salesperson license.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(3)(a); NREC Pre-License Education requirements sheet

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(5) requires all real estate license applicants in Nebraska — salesperson and broker alike — to complete a 6-clock-hour course in which subject, assigned course number 0003?
explanation: Every Nebraska license applicant, whether pursuing a salesperson's or broker's license, must complete a 6-hour Professional Practice and Standards course, which the Commission has designated course number 0003. It is a mandatory component layered on top of the core pre-license curriculum for each license type.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(5); NREC Pre-License Education requirements sheet

question: A broker applicant who already completed the 6-hour Professional Practice and Standards course (#0003) while earning a Nebraska salesperson's license must, according to NREC pre-license education guidance...
choice_a: Not repeat the course — it satisfies the broker requirement as well
choice_b: Retake the course as part of the additional 60 broker hours
choice_c: Retake only half of the course (3 hours)
explanation: NREC's pre-license education guidance explicitly notes that the Professional Practice and Standards course (#0003) does not need to be repeated for the broker license if it was already taken to qualify for the salesperson's license. The course is a one-time requirement that carries forward.
source_note: NREC Pre-License Education requirements sheet (implementing Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(5))

question: Per Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(2) and (5), what is the total number of pre-license education clock hours a Nebraska real estate salesperson applicant must complete (including the Professional Practice and Standards course)?
explanation: Nebraska salesperson applicants must complete 90 clock hours across three approved pre-license courses, plus the separate 6-hour Professional Practice and Standards course (#0003), for a total of 96 clock hours before sitting for the salesperson examination.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(2), (5); NREC Pre-License Education requirements sheet

question: The 90-hour Nebraska salesperson pre-license curriculum (excluding the Professional Practice and Standards course) is divided into three 30-hour courses. Which of the following is one of those required courses?
explanation: The 90-hour salesperson curriculum consists of three 30-hour courses: Real Estate Principles and Practices, Nebraska Real Estate License Law, and an additional Commission-approved pre-license education course. Property management, trust accounting, and team leadership are separate continuing-education or post-license topics, not part of this base curriculum.
source_note: NREC Pre-License Education requirements sheet (implementing Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(2))

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(1)(a), what is the minimum age a person must have attained before a Nebraska broker's or salesperson's license may be issued?
explanation: Nebraska law bars issuance of either a broker's or a salesperson's license to anyone who has not attained the age of nineteen years. This is an eligibility floor that applies before any education, experience, or examination requirements are even considered.

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(1)(b) conditions licensure on the applicant having...
choice_a: A high school diploma or its equivalent (or an exempt/home-school equivalent)
choice_b: A bachelor's degree from an accredited institution
choice_c: At least two years of college coursework
explanation: Nebraska requires license applicants to have graduated high school or hold an equivalent credential, with exceptions for graduates of programs exempted by the State Department of Education or otherwise acceptable educational programs (such as documented home-school participation). No college degree is required by the Act.

question: Under the hardship provision referenced in Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(3)(b), a broker applicant who cannot satisfy the standard licensed-experience requirement may petition the Commission for approval based on completion of which alternative?
choice_a: An additional 12 hours of continuing education
choice_b: Eighteen semester credit hours from an accredited college or university, or 180 classroom hours in real estate subjects
choice_c: A letter of recommendation from three licensed brokers
choice_d: Five years of any real-estate-adjacent employment
explanation: The Nebraska Real Estate License Act allows the Commission, through a special hearing, to approve an alternative path for broker applicants who cannot meet the standard two-year licensed-experience requirement. That alternative requires showing completion of either 18 semester credit hours in real estate related subjects from an accredited college or university, or 180 classroom hours of real estate coursework.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(3)(b); NREC Broker Hardship Provision Information

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(4), what consequence can result if a check or electronic payment submitted to the Commission for an original or renewal license fee, or an examination fee, is not honored?
choice_a: A $10 processing fee is automatically added with no other consequence
choice_b: The application is placed on a 90-day hold with no further action
choice_c: It is cause for revocation or denial of the license
choice_d: The applicant is barred from reapplying for five years
explanation: The statute treats a returned check or a rejected electronic payment used to pay an original license, renewal license, or examination fee as cause for the Commission to revoke or deny the license. The Fee Schedule separately assesses a $30.00 Returned Check Processing Fee and a $30.00 Not Accepted Fee in these situations.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(4); NREC Fee Schedule

question: According to Nebraska Real Estate Commission licensing information, what minimum score must a broker applicant achieve on the state licensing examination to pass?
explanation: The Nebraska Real Estate Commission's broker license information identifies a passing score of 75% on the state licensing examination as one of the 'other qualifications' an applicant must meet, alongside approval of the application and a current criminal history report.
source_note: NREC Resident Broker License Information sheet

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(7) requires Nebraska license applicants to submit to fingerprinting and an FBI criminal history record information check. Who bears the cost of this check?
choice_b: The Nebraska Real Estate Commission, from the State Real Estate Commission's Fund
choice_d: It is split evenly between the applicant and the Commission
explanation: The statute requires fingerprinting and a criminal history background check through the FBI as a condition of licensure, and places the cost of that check on the applicant, not on the Commission or a sponsoring broker.

question: Per Nebraska Real Estate Commission licensing guidance, what happens if a broker applicant's license is not issued within 30 days after they pass the state licensing examination?
choice_a: The application fee is automatically refunded
choice_b: The applicant must retake the real estate examination
choice_c: The applicant is granted an automatic 90-day extension
choice_d: Nothing — there is no such deadline
explanation: NREC's Resident Broker License Summary Checklist warns applicants that their license must be issued within 30 days of passing the examination, or they will have to retake the real estate examination. This makes timely completion of remaining steps — such as errors and omissions insurance and the license issuance form and fee — important once the exam is passed.
source_note: NREC Resident Real Estate Broker License Summary Checklist

question: How long is a Nebraska real estate license application and its accompanying criminal history background report valid, according to NREC checklist guidance, before the applicant must reapply if not yet licensed?
explanation: NREC's broker and license-recognition checklists both caution applicants that an application and its background report are valid for only one year from the date the application is received. If the applicant is not licensed by that date, they must reapply and, typically, resubmit fingerprints and fees.
source_note: NREC Resident Real Estate Broker License Summary Checklist

question: What is the current Nebraska Real Estate Commission License Application Fee for both salespersons and brokers?
explanation: The Commission's current fee schedule lists a single License Application Fee of $175.00 that applies to both salesperson and broker applicants, separate from the examination fee and the original license fee charged after passing the exam.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(1)

question: What is the current per-exam License Examination Fee charged by the Nebraska Real Estate Commission for salespersons and brokers?
explanation: The current NREC Fee Schedule lists a License Examination Fee of $150.00 per exam for both salespersons and brokers, distinct from the $175.00 License Application Fee and the $150.00 Examination Retake Fee.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(1)

question: A Nebraska broker applicant who fails the state licensing exam and retakes it within one year of their original application must pay an Examination Retake Fee of...
explanation: The NREC Fee Schedule sets the Examination Retake Fee at $150.00 for salespersons and brokers retaking the exam within one year of their application, the same amount as the original per-exam License Examination Fee.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(1)

question: What is the current Nebraska Real Estate Commission Broker Original License Fee (for the current year only)?
explanation: Once a broker applicant has passed the exam and been approved, NREC charges a Broker Original License Fee of $110.00, covering the current year only, which is separate from the two-year Broker Renewal Fee charged at subsequent renewals.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(1)

question: What is the current Nebraska Real Estate Commission Salesperson Original License Fee (for the current year only)?
explanation: NREC charges a Salesperson Original License Fee of $90.00, applicable to the current year only, which is lower than the corresponding $110.00 Broker Original License Fee — a distinction broker candidates should recognize since it also applied when they first licensed as a salesperson.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(1)

question: What is the current Nebraska Real Estate Commission two-year Broker Renewal Fee?
explanation: The Broker Renewal Fee, covering the standard two-year renewal cycle, is currently set at $220.00 — higher than both the $110.00 Broker Original License Fee and the $180.00 Salesperson Renewal Fee.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(3)

question: What is the current Nebraska Real Estate Commission two-year Salesperson Renewal Fee?
explanation: The Salesperson Renewal Fee for the standard two-year cycle is $180.00, which is $40 less than the $220.00 Broker Renewal Fee, reflecting the generally lower fee tier applied to salespersons throughout the Fee Schedule.
source_note: NREC Fee Schedule (updated January 2026), authorized under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(3)

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(3), Nebraska broker and salesperson renewal applications and fees are due on or before what date each renewal year, after which failure to pay automatically cancels the license on December 31?
explanation: The statute sets November 30 of each renewal year as the deadline for submitting the renewal application and fee. If a licensee fails to remit the renewal fee by that date, the license is automatically cancelled on December 31 of the renewal year, although a late renewal option remains available before the following July 1.

question: A Nebraska licensee who misses the renewal deadline may still file a late renewal application before July 1 of the following year, but must pay the standard renewal fee plus a late penalty of how much, per Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(3)?
choice_d: $25 for each month or fraction of a month late
explanation: The statute and the current NREC Fee Schedule impose a Late Renewal Penalty Fee of $25.00 for each month, or fraction of a month, beginning December 2, in addition to the regular renewal fee. The late renewal application itself must still be filed before July 1 of the ensuing year or the license lapses entirely.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.14(3); NREC Fee Schedule

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19(2), the Nebraska Real Estate Commission may charge an annual branch office license fee of not more than...
explanation: A broker who operates more than one place of business within Nebraska must obtain a branch office license for each additional location, managed by a broker or associate broker. The statute caps the annual branch office license fee at $50.00, which is also the amount currently charged for both the original Branch License Fee and the Branch Renewal Fee.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.19(2); NREC Fee Schedule

question: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.20(3) authorizes the Commission to charge a transfer fee, not to exceed a statutory cap, when a salesperson or associate broker transfers between employing brokers or changes status between broker and associate broker. What is that statutory cap (and the fee the Commission currently charges)?
explanation: Under §81-885.20(3), a transfer fee of not more than $50.00 applies when a salesperson or associate broker moves from one employing broker to another, or when a broker's affiliation status changes between broker and associate broker. The current NREC Fee Schedule sets this Transfer Fee at the full $50.00 statutory cap.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.20(3); NREC Fee Schedule

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51, how many clock hours of continuing education must an active Nebraska licensee complete during each two-year renewal cycle?
explanation: Active Nebraska licensees must complete 18 clock hours of continuing education as part of each two-year renewal cycle. This total is further broken down into Commission-approved continuing education hours and Commission-approved training hours.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51; NREC Continuing Education Requirements sheet

question: Of the 18 total continuing education clock hours Nebraska licensees must complete every two years, at least how many must be Commission-approved continuing education?
explanation: At least 12 of the 18 required continuing education hours must be Commission-approved continuing education, leaving up to 6 hours that may instead be satisfied through Commission-approved training toward the overall 18-hour requirement.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51; NREC Continuing Education Requirements sheet

question: Of the 12 Commission-approved continuing education hours Nebraska licensees must complete, at least how many must consist of designated required subject-matter courses marked with an 'R'?
explanation: Within the 12 hours of Commission-approved continuing education, at least 6 hours must come from courses designated with an 'R' for required subject matter. Duplicated continuing education content is generally prohibited within a four-year span, with limited exceptions for certain required 'R' courses in later cycles.
source_note: NREC Continuing Education Requirements sheet (implementing Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51)

question: Toward the 18-hour Nebraska continuing education total, up to how many hours may consist of Commission-approved training (as distinguished from Commission-approved continuing education courses)?
explanation: Up to 6 of the 18 required hours may be satisfied through Commission-approved training, complementing the at-least-12-hour Commission-approved continuing education requirement (of which at least 6 hours must be 'R' designated).
source_note: NREC Continuing Education Requirements sheet (implementing Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51)

question: A Nebraska licensee who is issued their license and renews it during that same calendar year is exempt from continuing education for...
choice_b: The first five years of licensure
choice_d: Nothing — new licensees must still complete full CE for the first cycle
explanation: New licensees who renew during the same calendar year in which their license was issued are exempt from continuing education requirements for that first renewal cycle only. For example, a licensee first licensed in 2026 renews for a two-year term in 2026 but is not required to complete continuing education until the 2028 renewal.
source_note: NREC Continuing Education Requirements sheet

question: A Nebraska licensee who resides in and is licensed by another jurisdiction may satisfy Nebraska's continuing education requirement by...
choice_a: Completing double the required Nebraska hours
choice_b: Being permanently exempt from all CE
choice_c: Submitting a notarized letter from their broker instead of CE certificates
choice_d: Affirming that they have met the continuing education requirement of their resident jurisdiction
explanation: Nonresident licensees and those licensed through license recognition may meet Nebraska's continuing education requirement by affirming that they have already satisfied the continuing education requirement of their resident jurisdiction, rather than separately completing Nebraska-specific coursework.
source_note: NREC Continuing Education Requirements sheet

question: Of the 12 hours of Commission-approved continuing education required under §81-885.51, licensees who provide or supervise property management services must complete how many hours in an approved property management course each two-year period?
explanation: Licensees who provide property management services, or who supervise a licensee who does, must complete 3 hours of approved property management coursework within each two-year period, carved out of the 12 hours of Commission-approved continuing education. These courses carry a 'PM' designation in the four-digit course number, and courses marked 'RPM' can satisfy both the property management and the 'R' required-subject requirements simultaneously.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51; NREC Property Management Education Requirements sheet

question: Nebraska licensees who are team members, team leaders, or designated brokers supervising a team must complete 3 hours of Commission-approved team/team-leadership education within how many days of being designated to that role or of the team's creation, with one such course (numbered 1000R) required every four years?
explanation: Team members, team leaders, and designated brokers who supervise a team must complete 3 hours of Commission-approved team or team-leadership coursework within 180 days of being designated to that role, or within 180 days of the team's creation for a supervising broker. A specific course numbered 1000R must be taken every four years as part of this requirement.
source_note: NREC Team Training Requirements sheet (implementing Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.51)

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(9)(a), all newly licensed Nebraska licensees must, within 180 days after license issuance, furnish evidence of completing how many hours of commission-approved post-license coursework (assigned course number 7000)?
explanation: Within 180 days after license issuance, every licensee must furnish satisfactory evidence of completing 12 hours of class study in a Commission-approved course covering required knowledge and skills — including contracts, listing agreements, and handling of client funds. This is course number 7000, and evidence of its completion remains valid for four years for any license application. Failure to comply places the license on inactive status until the requirement is met, with transfer back to active status subject to the fee under §81-885.20.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(9)(a)-(b); NREC Post-License Education sheet

question: Under Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(4), before a Nebraska broker may act as a designated broker supervising other licensees, they must complete post-licensure coursework (assigned course number 6000) covering trust accounting, brokerage finance, business ethics, and...
explanation: No person issued a broker's license may act as a designated broker for any other licensee until completing additional post-licensure coursework covering real estate trust accounting, brokerage finance, business ethics, and risk management. This is course number 6000. The Commission may extend the post-licensure coursework deadline by up to six months under the same hardship provision that applies to the experience requirement.
source_note: Neb. Rev. Stat. §81-885.13(4); NREC Designated Broker Additional Education Requirements sheet
